Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨x+xz,\,y,\,z-{x}^{2}⟩$ and the boundary $S$ of a spherical solid of radius $\sqrt{5}$ centered at the origin. Calculate the flux of $F$ through $S.$
worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

For a sphere or radius $r$ centered at $O,$ the unit normal to the sphere is given by

$$
n=\frac{⟨x,y,z⟩}{r}.
$$

In our case, we have $r=\sqrt{5}.$ Therefore,

$$
n=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨x,y,z⟩.
$$

Using the fact that ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=5$ on $S,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨x+xz,\,y,\,z-{x}^{2}⟩\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨x+xz,\,y,\,z-{x}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}(x(x+xz)+{y}^{2}+z(z-{x}^{2})) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}({x}^{2}+{x}^{2}z+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}-{x}^{2}z) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\cdot 5 \\  & =\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $F$ across $S$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}\sqrt{5}\,\text{d}S \\  & =\sqrt{5}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S \\  & =\sqrt{5}\cdot \text{Area}(S) \\  & =\sqrt{5}\cdot 4\pi \cdot (\sqrt{5})^{2} \\  & =20\pi \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$
